notes: Hastily documented at night and resealed; artifacts left in place. Entrance in the centre of the northern side. Inscribed ossuary (Hebrew, two lines). Similar kokhim caves nearby cited only.

features.subtype: rock-hewn kokhim cave: square chamber with standing pit and benches, six kokhim with sealing stones, lamp niches; seven ossuaries, one inscribed
features.period: 1st c. CE, most likely close to 70 CE
features.quote: it should be dated to the first century CE

title: Jerusalem, ʽAtarot, Beit Hanina Road
author: David Gellman
notes: Segment of the Roman–Byzantine Jerusalem–Bet Horon/Nablus road and a stone-filled streambed; no feature of the eligible classes.

title: Jerusalem, the Old City, The Churches Street
author: David Yeger
notes: Basement at 11 Churches Street: Mamluk structure and a late Ottoman liquid-extraction industry. Round plastered installation L8 with sump (industrial, not water storage) not coded.

features.subtype: cistern with stone-lined square shaft, probably incorporating an older underground cavity (interior not documented); courtyard cistern fed by a plastered channel; both later refuse pits
features.period: late Ottoman (Stratum I)
features.quote: containing an industrial installation, drainage channels and two water cisterns

features.subtype: plastered channels and clay-pipe gutters feeding the settling pit and cisterns
